sentences.en: It is my intention to give a full account of the first war between Rome and Carthage, which was fought for the possession of Sicily.
sentences.zh: 我打算详尽叙述罗马与迦太基之间的第一次战争，这场战争是为了争夺西西里岛的控制权而进行的。

sentences.en: This is because it would be hard to think of a conflict which went on for longer, demanded more effort from both sides, or was prosecuted with a
sentences.zh: 这是因为很难想象还有哪场冲突能持续如此之久，要求双方付出如此巨大的努力，或者以一种

sentences.en: more brutal vigour, nor one which featured more battles or more sudden changes of fortune.
sentences.zh: 更加残酷的力度进行，也没有哪场冲突包含更多的战役或更突如其来的命运转折。

sentences.en: The two cities which fought it were still at this time possessed of customs and institutions, that were yet to fall into decadence.
sentences.zh: 当时交战的两个城市仍然拥有尚未陷入颓废的习俗和制度。

sentences.en: Both were dependent chiefly on their own efforts rather than on good luck for their successes, and both were equally matched in terms of their resources,
sentences.zh: 两者在取得成功时，主要依赖自身的努力而非好运，且在资源方面势均力敌，

sentences.en: which is why we can arrive at a more accurate assessment of the respective qualities and
sentences.zh: 正因如此，我们才能比研究任何类似的冲突更准确地评估这场特定战争中

sentences.en: attributes of the two combatants in this particular war than we can by studying any comparable conflict.
sentences.zh: 两个交战方的各自素质和特质。

sentences.en: So that was the Greek writer Polybius talking about one of the titanic clashes not just in ancient history.
sentences.zh: 以上是希腊作家波利比乌斯对古代历史上不仅仅是其中一场泰坦级冲突的评价。

sentences.en: But Tom, in all history, it is the first Punic war between Rome and Carthage.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，在整个历史上，这是罗马和迦太基之间的第一次布匿战争。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I guess the Carthaginians would have called it the first Roman war.
sentences.zh: 我想迦太基人可能会称之为第一次罗马战争。

sentences.zh: 所以这或许是我们应该尝试记住的一个视角。

sentences.en: But yes, it is the great superpower clash in antiquity.
sentences.zh: 但没错，这是古代世界伟大的超级大国冲突。

sentences.en: Rome is essentially an upstart.

sentences.en: So that, I think, is what Polybius is talking about when he says that this is so interesting.

sentences.en: You can gauge the respective strengths of the two cities.

sentences.en: Maritime power, mercantile power, as you said.

sentences.zh: 罗马此时已经占领了整个意大利，吸收了拉齐奥以及所有其他人，比如坎帕尼亚等等，并将他们纳入了罗马体系，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 所以我们再次审视了各种和平条约是如何存在的。

sentences.zh: 它们曾是盟友，共同对抗这位

sentences.en: And he'd said,
sentences.zh: 他说过，

sentences.zh: 他们担心迦太基人可能会，你知道，他们拥有这支强大的舰队，他们对意大利海岸线的控制可能会使他们非常暴露。

sentences.en: But there's a very great scholar of Roman imperialism called William Harris, who makes a brilliantly convincing case that war

sentences.zh: 所以你赢得政治晋升，并在你的同胞面前赢得“荣誉”，即那种光荣的名声，是通过为你的城市取得伟大的成就。

sentences.en: And so that is kind of baked into the structure of Roman society.
sentences.zh: 所以这在某种程度上已经融入了罗马社会的结构中。

sentences.en: It has to be said that the Romans do not see themselves as predatory.
sentences.zh: 必须说，罗马人并不认为自己是掠夺性的。

sentences.en: They see themselves as a terribly moral people who essentially are going to war in self-defence.
sentences.zh: 他们认为自己是一个非常道德的民族，本质上是为了自卫而发动战争。

sentences.en: So there's this kind of weird thing that the Romans end up conquering the world effectively in self-defence.
sentences.zh: 所以有一种奇怪的事情，罗马人最终实际上是在自卫中征服了世界。

sentences.en: And they would say that the proof of the fact that they are a moral people is that the gods have favoured them and brought them victory.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，他们是道德民族的证据在于众神眷顾了他们并带给他们胜利。

sentences.en: So they don't see themselves as ruthless imperialists, although effectively that is what they are.
sentences.zh: 所以他们并不认为自己是无情的帝国主义者，尽管实际上他们就是这样。

sentences.en: But they are definitely a kind of new mutant element in this centuries-old conflict in Sicily between the Greeks and the Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 但他们绝对是西西里岛希腊人和迦太基人之间这场持续数世纪的冲突中一种新的突变因素。

sentences.en: And on top of that, of course, the Greeks and the Carthaginians are known factors to each other.
sentences.zh: 而且最重要的是，当然，希腊人和迦太基人彼此之间是已知的因素。

sentences.en: But I think Carthage also has reason to be hostile to Rome, actually.
sentences.zh: 但我认为迦太基实际上也有理由对罗马怀有敌意。

sentences.en: Because, of course, the Greeks are kind of known territory to the Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，希腊人对迦太基人来说是已知的领域。

sentences.en: They've been fighting them for so long.
sentences.zh: 他们已经和他们战斗了太久了。

sentences.en: But Rome is a kind of alarming and novel element of this.
sentences.zh: 但罗马是其中一种令人担忧且新颖的因素。

sentences.en: And so much later, there's a historian, Cassius Dio, writing about the build-up to the First Punic War.

sentences.en: And he says, the Carthaginians, who had been a great power for so long, and the Romans, who were growing ever stronger by the year, could not help

sentences.zh: 对彼此投以嫉妒的目光。

sentences.zh: 所以这就是今天美国地缘政治战略家所说的“修昔底德陷阱”。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 他使自己成为暴君，然后成为叙拉古国王。

sentences.en: Carthaginians don't know this.

sentences.zh: 所以迦太基人，他们进入了

sentences.zh: 而迦太基人感到被冒犯并要求罗马撤军的事实被视为不尊重。

sentences.en: And so the Romans are fully up for full scale war.
sentences.zh: 所以罗马人完全准备好进行全面战争了。

sentences.en: And the Carthaginians, because they are not prepared to tolerate the intrusion of this upstart power into their sphere of influence, likewise are completely committed to it.
sentences.zh: 而迦太基人，因为他们不准备容忍这个暴发户势力侵入他们的势力范围，同样也完全投入其中。

sentences.en: And the Carthaginians, although they respect Roman land forces, the Carthaginians are dependent on mercenaries.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人虽然尊重罗马的陆军，但迦太基人依赖雇佣兵。

sentences.en: They don't have this kind of great body of citizens that the Romans can command.
sentences.zh: 他们没有罗马人可以指挥的那种庞大的公民群体。

sentences.en: They're confident of victory because of course, Sicily is an island.
sentences.zh: 他们对胜利充满信心，因为当然，西西里岛是一个岛屿。

sentences.en: They are the great maritime power and the Romans don't have a fleet.
sentences.zh: 他们是伟大的海上强权，而罗马人没有舰队。

sentences.en: So Carthage thinks we can ace this.
sentences.zh: 所以迦太基认为我们可以搞定这个。

sentences.en: And so what they do, so there's a place, Lilibaeum, which is on the kind of the furthest most Western point.
sentences.zh: 所以他们所做的，有一个地方叫利利拜翁，位于最西端。

sentences.en: Panormus, which is Palermo, modern day Palermo.
sentences.zh: 帕诺尔穆斯，也就是巴勒莫，现代的巴勒莫。

sentences.en: Palermo is an old Phoenician city.
sentences.zh: 巴勒莫是一座古老的腓尼基城市。

sentences.en: Lilibaeum was deliberately founded to be an impregnable fortress of Carthaginian power.
sentences.zh: 利利拜翁被特意建立为迦太基权力的坚不可摧的堡垒。

sentences.en: But what they actually decide to do is to seize control of a Greek city, Akragas at modern day Agrigento, because it's further to the east on
sentences.zh: 但他们实际上决定做的是夺取一座希腊城市，阿克拉加斯，即现代的阿格里真托，因为它在南海岸更靠东。

sentences.en: the southern coaSt. So it's towards where the Romans are operating, but it can be easily supplied from Carthage.
sentences.zh: 所以它靠近罗马人的活动区域，但可以很容易地从迦太基获得补给。

sentences.en: It's a Greek city.
sentences.zh: 这是一座希腊城市。

sentences.en: It's famous for having been once ruled by a notorious tyrant who used to boil people to death inside a great bronze bull.
sentences.zh: 它以曾经被一位臭名昭著的暴君统治而闻名，他曾把人活活煮死在一个巨大的铜牛里。

sentences.en: And it's large and prosperous.
sentences.zh: 它很大且繁荣。

sentences.en: There are kind of maybe 25, 30,000 people there and they fortify it.
sentences.zh: 那里大约有25,000到30,000人，他们加固了它。

sentences.en: The Romans pile in, they besiege it.
sentences.zh: 罗马人蜂拥而至，围攻它。

sentences.en: Carthage sends a huge relief force, 60 elephants, all the works.
sentences.zh: 迦太基派出一支庞大的救援部队，60头大象，所有的一切。

sentences.en: And Dominic, I'm sure you can guess the name of the guy in charge of it.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我相信你能猜出负责人的名字。

sentences.en: He's yet another Hanno, is he?
sentences.zh: 又是另一个汉诺，是吗？

sentences.en: He is a Hanno.
sentences.zh: 他确实是汉诺。

sentences.en: He's yet another Hanno.
sentences.zh: 又是另一个汉诺。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But this is a terrible, he's a terrible general.
sentences.zh: 但这太糟糕了，他是个糟糕的将军。

sentences.en: So he lands with his forces and he looks down from a hill at the Romans.
sentences.zh: 于是他带着部队登陆，从山上俯瞰罗马军队。

sentences.en: And he thinks, oh, I don't really want to fight them.
sentences.zh: 他心想，噢，我其实不太想跟他们打。

sentences.en: A bit nervous of it.
sentences.zh: 有点发怵。

sentences.en: So he just stays there for two months.
sentences.zh: 所以他就在那儿待了两个月。

sentences.en: And then finally, because we should say, we mentioned this a couple of episodes ago, but the penalty for failure in Carthage is very, very severe.
sentences.zh: 最后，我们之前几集提到过，迦太基对失败的惩罚非常非常严厉。

sentences.en: So at the worst, you can be crucified, but you know, it's not good.
sentences.zh: 最坏的情况可能会被钉死在十字架上，总之不是什么好事。

sentences.en: So finally he thinks, well, I better crack on.
sentences.zh: 所以他最终想，好吧，我还是得硬着头皮上。

sentences.en: So he advances against the Romans, but it's a disaster.
sentences.zh: 于是他向罗马军队发起进攻，但结果是一场灾难。

sentences.en: The Romans stand firm, the elephants stampede, they trample their own men.
sentences.zh: 罗马人阵脚稳固，大象受惊乱窜，踩踏了自己人。

sentences.en: It's a complete catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 简直是一场彻底的灾难。

sentences.en: And the commander of the Carthaginian garrison in Acragas realises that all is loSt. And so he and his garrison slip out.
sentences.zh: 阿格里真托的迦太基守军指挥官意识到大势已去，于是他和守军悄悄撤离了。

sentences.en: They fill the Roman trenches with straw, managed to get across Scarpa.
sentences.zh: 他们用稻草填平了罗马人的战壕，成功穿过了斯卡帕。

sentences.en: The Romans move into Acragas, sack it, sell all its inhabitants into slavery.
sentences.zh: 罗马人进入阿格里真托，洗劫了城市，并将所有居民卖为奴隶。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, back in Carthage, Hanno loses all his civil rights and has a massive fine slapped on him.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在迦太基，汉诺被剥夺了所有公民权利，还被处以巨额罚款。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Could have been worse.
sentences.zh: 本来可能会更糟的。

sentences.en: Could have been crucified.
sentences.zh: 本来可能会被钉死在十字架上的。

sentences.en: Yeah, it absolutely could have been worse.
sentences.zh: 是啊，绝对可能会更糟。

sentences.en: And back in Rome, the news that they have brushed off the Carthaginians so easily kind of determines
sentences.zh: 回到罗马，他们如此轻易地击退了迦太基人的消息，某种程度上坚定了

sentences.en: them in their conviction that they should kick the Carthaginians out of Sicily altogether.
sentences.zh: 他们将迦太基人彻底赶出西西里的决心。

sentences.en: The Carthaginians, they rely very heavily on mercenaries, don't they?
sentences.zh: 迦太基人非常依赖雇佣兵，对吧？

sentences.en: So even at this stage, they rely on some mercenaries in a way the Romans aren't?
sentences.zh: 所以即使在这个阶段，他们也在以一种罗马人没有的方式依赖雇佣兵？

sentences.en: Yeah, basically their troops are all mercenaries.
sentences.zh: 是的，基本上他们的部队全都是雇佣兵。

sentences.en: So obviously the problem though for the Romans is that if they're going to conquer Sicily, let alone hold it, they do need a fleet.
sentences.zh: 显然，罗马人面临的问题是，如果他们想征服西西里，更不用说守住它，他们确实需要一支舰队。

sentences.en: And this, you know, this is a real challenge because Carthage is the greatest naval power of its day.
sentences.zh: 这可是个真正的挑战，因为迦太基是当时最强大的海军强国。

sentences.en: It's got centuries of maritime experience.
sentences.zh: 它拥有数百年的海上经验。

sentences.en: It's the inventor, Dominic, of the Quadrarim, which is a ship that is bigger and more powerful than the Trireme.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，它是四层桨战船的发明者，这种船比三层桨战船更大、更强大。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it has kind of four banks of oars.
sentences.zh: 所以它有四排桨。

sentences.en: And it also has lots of quincarims, which is battleships with five bounds of oars, which had been invented by the Syracusans.
sentences.zh: 而且它还有很多五层桨战船，也就是有五排桨的战舰，这是叙拉古人发明的。

sentences.en: So they're basically the kind of the dreadnoughts of the ancient world.
sentences.zh: 所以它们基本上就是古代世界的“无畏舰”。

sentences.en: And the Romans don't have any of these, but this is exactly the kind of challenge the Romans relish.
sentences.zh: 罗马人虽然没有这些船，但这正是罗马人乐于接受的挑战。

sentences.en: So a quincarim has been shipwrecked on the Italian coast, the Carthaginian quincarim.
sentences.zh: 当时有一艘迦太基的五层桨战船在意大利海岸失事了。

sentences.en: So they take it and they disassemble it because the way the Carthaginians build ships, and we know this because the shipwreck of one of them has been found, they kind of built
sentences.zh: 于是他们把它拖过来拆解，因为我们知道迦太基人建造船只的方式——因为已经发现了一艘失事船只——他们建造

sentences.en: them in the way that you might build a cabinet from Ikea.
sentences.zh: 它们的方式就像你组装宜家家具一样。

sentences.en: They're kind of flat packs, they're kind of numbered pieces and you can stick them all together.
sentences.zh: 它们就像是平板包装，有编号的零件，你可以把它们拼在一起。

sentences.en: And so this actually makes it quite easy for the Romans to work out how to build.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上让罗马人很容易弄清楚该怎么造。

sentences.en: Oh, just to copy it.
sentences.zh: 噢，就是照着抄。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Just to copy it.
sentences.zh: 就是照着抄。

sentences.en: And so they do this and they build a hundred quincarims, 20 triremes and
sentences.zh: 于是他们照做了，造了一百艘五层桨战船、二十艘三层桨战船，

sentences.en: Polybius, you know, our Greek historian, who's our main source for this, terribly impressed.
sentences.zh: 波利比乌斯，也就是我们那位希腊历史学家，我们关于此的主要资料来源，对此印象深刻。

sentences.en: And he says of this, that nothing better illustrates the remarkable spirit and boldness of the Romans.
sentences.zh: 他评价说，没有什么比这更能体现罗马人非凡的精神和胆识了。

sentences.en: And so they build this great fleet.
sentences.zh: 于是他们建立起了这支伟大的舰队。

sentences.en: None of the Romans have any naval experience at all, but they kind of go sailing down to try and confront the Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 罗马人完全没有任何海军经验，但他们还是出海去试图对抗迦太基人。

sentences.en: And it's an absolute disaster.
sentences.zh: 结果是一场彻底的灾难。

sentences.en: They sail into an enemy harbour.
sentences.zh: 他们驶入敌方港口。

sentences.en: The Carthaginians come out, all the crews panic, jump into the sea and the whole force is taken prisoner.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人冲出来，所有船员惊慌失措，跳进海里，整支部队都被俘虏了。

sentences.en: But does this put the Romans off?
sentences.zh: 但这会让罗马人退缩吗？

sentences.en: Probably not.
sentences.zh: 大概不会。

sentences.en: No, it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 不，并没有。

sentences.en: Because the Romans realise that they're never going to be able to match the Carthaginians in terms of their mobility, you know, the art of ramming a ship, of all that
sentences.zh: 因为罗马人意识到，他们在机动性方面，也就是撞击船只的艺术，以及所有那类

sentences.en: kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 事情上，永远无法与迦太基人相比。

sentences.en: But what the Romans are really good at is, of course, fighting on land.
sentences.zh: 但罗马人真正擅长的，当然是陆战。

sentences.en: And so the Roman wheeze is to turn naval battles into land battles.
sentences.zh: 所以罗马人的妙计就是把海战变成陆战。

sentences.en: And they do this by inventing a thing they call the Corvus, which is a crow.
sentences.zh: 他们通过发明一种叫“乌鸦吊桥”的东西来实现这一点。

sentences.en: So it's a kind of boarding bridge that has a huge, great spike on the end.
sentences.zh: 它是一种登船桥，末端有一个巨大的尖刺。

sentences.en: So like the beak of a, you know, a crow or a raven.
sentences.zh: 就像乌鸦或渡鸦的喙一样。

sentences.en: And you sail up beside the enemy ship and you release this and the spike sinks into the boards of the enemy ship.
sentences.zh: 你把船开到敌舰旁边，放下这个装置，尖刺就会扎进敌舰的甲板里。

sentences.en: And then all your, you know, your soldiers, your marines can pile across, slaughter the enemy and seize control of the enemy ship.
sentences.zh: 然后你所有的士兵、海军陆战队员就可以冲过去，屠杀敌人并夺取敌舰的控制权。

sentences.en: It's a brilliant invention.
sentences.zh: 这是一个天才的发明。

sentences.en: No one's thought of it before.
sentences.zh: 以前没人想到过。

sentences.en: And so the Romans, very excited, they sail out.
sentences.zh: 于是罗马人非常兴奋，他们出航了。

sentences.en: And in 260, they creep up on the Carthaginian fleet, who have no idea what's about to hit them, at a place called Mylai off northern Sicily.
sentences.zh: 公元前260年，他们在西西里岛北部的米莱，悄悄接近了完全不知道大难临头的迦太基舰队。

sentences.en: And it's a tremendous success.
sentences.zh: 那是一次巨大的成功。

sentences.en: They win.
sentences.zh: 他们赢了。

sentences.en: And again,
sentences.zh: 而且再次，

sentences.en: Polybius says it's that the battle became exactly like a battle on land.
sentences.zh: 波利比乌斯说，这场战斗变得和陆战一模一样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So they've turned it into the kind of battle that they know and are very proficient at.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把它变成了他们所熟悉且非常擅长的战斗方式。

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And for the Carthaginians, you can imagine this is a tremendous shock to be beaten by a bunch of landlubbers.
sentences.zh: 对于迦太基人来说，你可以想象，被一群旱鸭子打败是一个巨大的打击。

sentences.en: And so the remnants of the Carthaginian fleet sail off to
sentences.zh: 于是迦太基舰队的残部逃往了

sentences.en: Sardinia.
sentences.zh: 撒丁岛。

sentences.en: And they're so pissed off with the Carthaginian admiral.
sentences.zh: 他们对那位迦太基海军上将非常恼火。

sentences.en: They don't find him, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，他们没找他算账。

sentences.en: They don't deprive him of his civic rights.
sentences.zh: 他们没有剥夺他的公民权利。

sentences.en: They crucify him.
sentences.zh: 他们把他钉死在了十字架上。

sentences.en: And Tom, as you've noted there, this is a battle referred to in T.S.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，正如你刚才提到的，这场战斗在T.S.

sentences.en: Eliot's The Wasteland.
sentences.zh: 艾略特的《荒原》中被提及。

sentences.en: Yes, very sinister passage.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常阴森的一段。

sentences.en: The first part of it, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是第一部分，对吧？

sentences.en: Stetson, you who were with me in the ships at Mylai, that corpse you planted last year in your garden, has it begun to sprout?
sentences.zh: “斯泰森，你我曾在米莱同船作战，去年你种在花园里的那具尸体，它发芽了吗？”

sentences.en: I wonder why.
sentences.zh: 我想知道为什么。

sentences.en: Well, I don't know why T.S.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道为什么T.S.

sentences.en: Eliot chose that particular battle.
sentences.zh: 艾略特选择了那场特定的战斗。

sentences.en: Do you know, Tom?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: I think because the scale of slaughter and fighting in this war must have reminded Eliot of the scale of slaughter in the First World War, the horror of it.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为这场战争中屠杀和战斗的规模，一定让艾略特想起了第一次世界大战中屠杀的规模，那种恐怖感。

sentences.en: And it just goes on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 而且它没完没了。

sentences.en: Because even though, you know, Mylai is a great victory, but it doesn't bring the Carthaginians to defeat at all.
sentences.zh: 因为尽管米莱是一场伟大的胜利，但它根本没有让迦太基人彻底战败。

sentences.en: Because weirdly, despite the fact the Romans have now won at sea, they're actually doing quite badly in the land war in Sicily.
sentences.zh: 因为奇怪的是，尽管罗马人现在在海上赢了，但他们在西西里的陆战中实际上打得很糟糕。

sentences.en: Because the Carthaginians, just as the Romans have learned how to fight on the sea, the Carthaginians have learned how to fight the Romans on land.
sentences.zh: 因为迦太基人，就像罗马人学会了如何进行海战一样，迦太基人也学会了如何在陆地上对付罗马人。

sentences.en: And they do it by avoiding pitch battle, by adopting guerrilla tactics.
sentences.zh: 他们通过避免正面交锋，采取游击战术来做到这一点。

sentences.en: And the Romans, a bit like the Americans in Vietnam, or, you know, European colonial powers, get so cross with this that they start conducting reprisals against local populations.
sentences.zh: 而罗马人，有点像越南战争中的美国人，或者欧洲殖民列强，对此感到非常愤怒，以至于他们开始对当地民众进行报复。

sentences.en: They lose hearts and minds.
sentences.zh: 他们失去了民心。

sentences.en: And their control over Greek Sicily starts to kind of to wobble.
sentences.zh: 他们对希腊化西西里的控制开始动摇。

sentences.en: And so in 256, that's four years after Mylai, they decide to do what the Romans have always been good at, which is going for the jugular.
sentences.zh: 于是在公元前256年，也就是米莱之战四年后，他们决定做罗马人一直擅长的事，那就是直捣黄龙。

sentences.en: And they decide to follow the example that had been set by Agathocles, the Syracuse and tyrant who had invaded Africa, and launch a full-blown invasion of Carthage.
sentences.zh: 他们决定效仿叙拉古暴君阿加托克利斯入侵非洲的先例，对迦太基发动全面入侵。

sentences.en: They've got by now 330 ships, and they load these ships with 140,000 men.
sentences.zh: 当时他们拥有330艘战船，并装载了14万名士兵。

sentences.en: Both the consuls are in charge of this great armada, sails across the Mediterranean towards Africa, and the Carthaginians sail out to oppose them with a fleet that has 150,000 men.
sentences.zh: 两位执政官负责指挥这支庞大的舰队，横渡地中海驶向非洲，而迦太基人则派出一支拥有15万人的舰队进行阻击。

sentences.en: Can we rely on these numbers, or are these made up according to the Roman sort of literary practice of inflation?
sentences.zh: 我们能相信这些数字吗？还是说这些数字是根据罗马文学中那种夸大的惯例编造的？

sentences.en: I think we probably can.
sentences.zh: 我想我们大概可以相信。

sentences.en: And even if they're not precise, they reflect a fact, that is noted by Greeks at the time, and gets kind of reported by Polybius, our favourite
sentences.zh: 即使它们不精确，也反映了一个事实，当时希腊人注意到了这一点，并被我们最喜欢的

sentences.en: Greek source.
sentences.zh: 希腊资料来源波利比乌斯记录了下来。

sentences.en: It's seen as being a battle beyond the dreams of people in the eastern half of the
sentences.zh: 这被视为一场超乎地中海东部人民想象的战斗。

sentences.en: Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 所以希腊世界习惯于认为自己才是大国。

sentences.en: So that the Greek world is accustomed to think of itself as these are the great powers.
sentences.zh: 而现在突然传来了这场战斗的消息，其规模之大超出了他们所能理解的范畴。

sentences.en: And now suddenly they're getting reports of this battle, which is on a scale larger than anything they could comprehend.
sentences.zh: 这总让我想起第二次世界大战中美国和日本舰队之间的中途岛海战，以及欧洲人当时一定觉得这是完全不同量级的冲突。

sentences.en: On the other side of the tables was a Libyan of colossal stature with short black curly hair.
sentences.zh: 桌子的另一边坐着一个身材魁梧的利比亚人，留着黑色短卷发。

sentences.en: He had retained only his military jacket, the brass plates of which were tearing the purple of the couch.
sentences.zh: 他只保留了军装上衣，上面的铜片把紫色的长榻都划破了。

sentences.en: A necklace of silver moons was tangled in his hairy breaSt.
sentences.zh: 一串银月项链缠在他多毛的胸口。

sentences.en: His face was stained with splashes of blood.
sentences.zh: 他的脸上沾满了血迹。

sentences.en: He was leaning on his left elbow with a smile on his large open mouth.
sentences.zh: 他用左肘支撑着身体，大嘴张开，带着微笑。

sentences.en: So that is what Matho is like.
sentences.zh: 这就是马托的样子。

sentences.en: That is what Matho is like.
sentences.zh: 这就是马托的样子。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's hairy, he's huge, he's smiling and he's covered in blood.
sentences.zh: 是的，他毛发浓密，身材高大，面带微笑，浑身是血。

sentences.en: He rips couches, all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他撕裂长榻，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So Spendius and Matho have essentially got the mercenaries behind them.
sentences.zh: 所以斯彭迪乌斯和马托基本上已经控制了雇佣兵。

sentences.en: They've said, look, let's conquer Carthage and take it all, take it over.
sentences.zh: 他们说，看，让我们征服迦太基，夺取一切，接管它。

sentences.en: They are duly appointed generals of the mercenary force.
sentences.zh: 他们被正式任命为雇佣军的将军。

sentences.en: And so when Gisco comes, they say, let's take him prisoner.
sentences.zh: 所以当吉斯戈来的时候，他们说，把他抓起来。

sentences.en: So they take him prisoner and they seize all the gold that's been sent and they remint it.
sentences.zh: 于是他们把他抓了起来，夺取了送来的所有黄金，并重新铸造了它们。

sentences.en: So this is Carthaginian coinage.
sentences.zh: 所以这是迦太基的货币。

sentences.en: The mercenaries remint it and they're stamping it and they're kind of saying that they're a kind of proto-state.
sentences.zh: 雇佣兵重新铸造了它，并在上面盖章，他们说他们是一种原始国家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there are 20,000 mercenaries.
sentences.zh: 而且有两万名雇佣兵。

sentences.en: And because of Matho, this giant hairy Libyan, they are able to raise maybe up to kind of 70,000 Libyans from the interior beyond Carthage.
sentences.zh: 因为马托这个毛发浓密的利比亚巨人，他们能够从迦太基以外的内陆地区召集多达7万名利比亚人。

sentences.en: So this is, you know, almost 100,000 troops, you know, and the Carthaginians don't really have the men to oppose them.
sentences.zh: 所以这，你知道，几乎有10万军队，你知道，而迦太基人真的没有兵力来对抗他们。

sentences.en: They don't have any.
sentences.zh: 他们一个都没有。

sentences.en: Yeah, they don't.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们没有。

sentences.en: I love this.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: I love the mercenary war.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢雇佣兵战争。

sentences.en: I love Salombo, which I did at university.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢《萨朗波》，我在大学时读过。

sentences.en: And basically it's just unbelievably sadistic and blood-soaked, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 基本上它简直是令人难以置信的残忍和血腥，不是吗？

sentences.en: What follows?
sentences.zh: 接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Absolutely hideous.
sentences.zh: 绝对恐怖。

sentences.en: And Polybius says that this is, of all wars, the war in which the greatest atrocities and cruelties were practised.
sentences.zh: 波利比乌斯说，在所有的战争中，这是最残暴、最残酷的一场。

sentences.en: And in part, that is because the mercenaries know that by taking this step, you know, if they're defeated, they can expect no mercy.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这是因为雇佣兵知道，采取这一步，你知道，如果他们失败了，他们将得不到任何怜悯。

sentences.en: But likewise, Carthage knows that she is fighting for her very survival.
sentences.zh: 同样，迦太基也知道她是在为生存而战。

sentences.en: So what are you going to do if you're Carthage and you're fighting for your very survival?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你是迦太基，正在为生存而战，你会怎么做？

sentences.en: Obviously, you're going to turn to a Hanno.
sentences.zh: 显然，你会求助于汉诺。

sentences.en: This is what you do in this situation, despite the fact that as far as like, you know, from the records, every time a Hanno leads something, they turn out to be terrible.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下你只能这么做，尽管事实上，据记录，每次汉诺领导什么，结果都糟透了。

sentences.en: They've never won with a Hanno, Tom.
sentences.zh: 他们从来没有在汉诺的带领下赢过，汤姆。

sentences.en: So this guy, he's called Hanno the Great.
sentences.zh: 所以这个家伙，他被称为“伟大的汉诺”。

sentences.en: And this is because he seems to have been the most significant political player in Carthage for the previous two decades.
sentences.zh: 这是因为他似乎是过去二十年来迦太基最重要的政治人物。

sentences.en: So while Hamilcar is the great military leader, Hanno seems to have been the political commander in chief.
sentences.zh: 所以虽然哈米尔卡是伟大的军事领袖，但汉诺似乎是政治总司令。

sentences.en: So he gets told, go out and defeat these mercenaries.
sentences.zh: 所以他被告知，去击败这些雇佣兵。

sentences.en: Predictably, he makes a complete hash of it.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，他把事情搞得一团糟。

sentences.en: And so the people say, well, Hanno's hopeless.
sentences.zh: 于是人们说，嗯，汉诺没救了。

sentences.en: Let's have Hamilcar.
sentences.zh: 让我们请哈米尔卡吧。

sentences.en: He's the military hero.
sentences.zh: 他是军事英雄。

sentences.en: Let's make him joint commander with Hanno.
sentences.zh: 让我们让他和汉诺共同指挥。

sentences.en: So he's given a very small army, only about 10,000 men, a few war elephants.
sentences.zh: 于是他只得到了一支很小的军队，大约只有1万人，还有几头战象。

sentences.en: But because he's a brilliant general, he's able to go out and win the victories that Hanno had been unable to.
sentences.zh: 但因为他是一位出色的将军，他能够出去赢得汉诺无法赢得的胜利。

sentences.en: And the mercenaries are defeated in a couple of battles.
sentences.zh: 雇佣兵在几次战斗中被击败了。

sentences.en: And in the camp, Spendius and Matho are nervous that this may lead to mass desertions.
sentences.zh: 在营地里，斯彭迪乌斯和马托很担心这会导致大规模的逃兵。

sentences.en: And so they decide to take a step that will effectively ensure that all the mercenaries are dipping their fingers in blood.
sentences.zh: 于是他们决定采取一步行动，确保所有的雇佣兵都沾上鲜血。

sentences.en: So what they do, contrary to all the laws of war, is that they put Gisco and the other Carthaginian members of the embassy to death.
sentences.zh: 所以他们所做的，违反了所有战争法，就是将吉斯戈和其他迦太基使团成员处死。

sentences.en: And they do it horribly.
sentences.zh: 而且他们做得非常残忍。

sentences.en: So what they do, they cut the hands off of Gisco and the other Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 他们砍掉了吉斯戈和其他迦太基人的手。

sentences.en: They castrate them.
sentences.zh: 他们阉割了他们。

sentences.en: And we haven't had some genital mutilation for a while.
sentences.zh: 我们已经有一段时间没有提到生殖器残割了。

sentences.en: And they then break their legs.
sentences.zh: 然后他们打断了他们的腿。

sentences.en: They throw them into a pit.
sentences.zh: 把他们扔进坑里。

sentences.en: And they then bury them alive.
sentences.zh: 然后把他们活埋了。

sentences.en: And the leaders of the mercenaries, so Spendius and Matho, then say that this is how all Carthaginian prisons of war will be treated.
sentences.zh: 雇佣兵的领袖，也就是斯彭迪乌斯和马托，随后声称所有迦太基战俘都将受到同样的对待。

sentences.en: So they really are making it impossible now to have any settlement.
sentences.zh: 所以他们现在真的让任何和解都变得不可能了。

sentences.en: It is absolutely a war to the death.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一场你死我活的战争。

sentences.en: And so Hamilcar reciprocates.
sentences.zh: 于是哈米尔卡也进行了报复。

sentences.en: If he captures any of the mercenaries, he has them trampled to death by elephants.
sentences.zh: 如果他俘虏了任何雇佣兵，他就让他们被大象踩死。

sentences.en: Hanno is still on the scene, but general acceptance is that he's so rubbish that in this war to the death, they need Hamilcar.
sentences.zh: 汉诺还在现场，但普遍的共识是他太无能了，在这场你死我活的战争中，他们需要哈米尔卡。

sentences.en: And so the troops, all the Carthaginian troops, vote for Hamilcar to be sole general.
sentences.zh: 于是部队，所有的迦太基部队，投票支持哈米尔卡担任唯一将军。

sentences.en: And this is obviously good because it means that the guy best qualified to win the war now has sole command.
sentences.zh: 这显然是好事，因为这意味着最有资格赢得战争的人现在拥有了唯一的指挥权。

sentences.en: And there are also two other positives.
sentences.zh: 还有另外两个积极因素。

sentences.en: And one is that help and reinforcements arrive from Carthage's old enemy Syracuse.
sentences.zh: 一是来自迦太基的老敌人叙拉古的援助和增援。

sentences.en: And the reason for this probably is that Hero, who is still in situ, you know, he's nervous about the Romans being too powerful.
sentences.zh: 其原因可能是希伦，他仍然在位，你知道，他担心罗马人势力过大。

sentences.en: So he wants Carthage to survive.
sentences.zh: 所以他希望迦太基生存下去。

sentences.en: So it will be a counterweight to the Romans.
sentences.zh: 这样它就能成为对抗罗马人的制衡力量。

sentences.en: But help also comes from Rome.
sentences.zh: 但援助也来自罗马。

sentences.en: So they release all the prisoners, Carthaginian prisoners that they'd been keeping without demanding a ransom.
sentences.zh: 他们释放了所有他们一直扣押的迦太基囚犯，没有要求任何赎金。

sentences.en: And they issue an absolutely strict ban that no one in Italy is allowed to help the mercenaries.
sentences.zh: 他们发布了一项绝对严格的禁令，禁止意大利境内的任何人帮助雇佣兵。

sentences.en: And again, you might think, well, why are they doing this to their old enemy?
sentences.zh: 同样，你可能会想，嗯，他们为什么要对老敌人这样做？

sentences.en: And the reason obviously is because they want Carthage to survive so that it can pay the indemnity.
sentences.zh: 显然，原因在于他们希望迦太基存续下去，这样它才能支付赔款。

sentences.en: So it's a little bit as if the Allies had intervened to help the Weimar Republic during the German Revolution or something.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像是协约国在德国革命期间干预并帮助魏玛共和国之类的做法。

sentences.en: Yes, I think that's exactly the analogy.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想这正是那个类比。

sentences.en: So things are starting to improve for Carthage.
sentences.zh: 所以迦太基的情况开始好转了。

sentences.en: And then in 238, so a couple of years after the outbreak of the revolt,
sentences.zh: 然后在公元前238年，也就是叛乱爆发几年后，

sentences.en: the great decisive moment comes when Hamilcar successfully traps a large chunk of the mercenary army in a narrow pass called the Soar.
sentences.zh: 伟大的决定性时刻到来了，哈米尔卡成功地将雇佣军的一大股主力困在了一个叫“索尔”的狭窄山口。

sentences.en: So it's called the Battle of the Soar.
sentences.zh: 所以它被称为“索尔之战”。

sentences.en: Yeah, Flaubert calls it the Defile of the Axe, which I think sounds better than the Soar.
sentences.zh: 是的，福楼拜称之为“斧头峡谷”，我觉得这听起来比“索尔”好听。

sentences.en: Yeah, Defile of the Axe is better, I agree.
sentences.zh: 是的，“斧头峡谷”更好，我同意。

sentences.en: Yeah, anyway, sorry, that's just by the by.
sentences.zh: 好吧，总之，抱歉，那只是顺带一提。

sentences.en: Well, let's call it the Defile of the Axe.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们就叫它“斧头峡谷”吧。

sentences.en: And Hamilcar blockades them, you know, and there's none of this Samnite thing of allowing them to go through a yoke or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 哈米尔卡封锁了他们，你知道的，这里可没有萨姆尼特人那种允许他们从轭下穿过之类的把戏。

sentences.en: Hamilcar, basically, he starves them out.
sentences.zh: 哈米尔卡基本上是把他们活活饿死了。

sentences.en: And so the mercenaries, they kill their prisoners, they kill their slaves, they eat them.
sentences.zh: 于是雇佣兵们杀死了他们的俘虏，杀死了他们的奴隶，把他们吃掉了。

sentences.en: And then once they've done that, they recognise that they've got no choice but to negotiate.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们这么做了，他们就意识到除了谈判别无选择。

sentences.en: And so Spendius had been in charge of this.
sentences.zh: 斯彭迪乌斯一直负责此事。

sentences.en: Matho is with the other army.
sentences.zh: 马托则在另一支军队那边。

sentences.en: So Spendius and nine other of the mercenaries go out to treat with Hamilcar.
sentences.zh: 于是斯彭迪乌斯和其他九名雇佣兵前去与哈米尔卡谈判。

sentences.en: And Hamilcar offers them what seem to be very mild terMs.
sentences.zh: 哈米尔卡向他们提出了看似非常温和的条件。

sentences.en: He says, yeah, fine, you can go.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，没问题，你们可以走。

sentences.en: The whole army can go, but you will need to leave me with ten hostages.
sentences.zh: 整支军队都可以走，但你们得给我留下十个人质。

sentences.en: And Spendius and his nine colleagues agree.
sentences.zh: 斯彭迪乌斯和他的九名同僚同意了。

sentences.en: And of course, the ten hostages that Hamilcar chooses is Spendius and the other nine negotiators.
sentences.zh: 当然，哈米尔卡选出的十个人质正是斯彭迪乌斯和其他九名谈判代表。

sentences.en: Very canny.
sentences.zh: 非常精明。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so he then, he seizes them, keeps them, fetters them up and then slaughters the entire army.
sentences.zh: 于是他抓住了他们，扣留了他们，给他们戴上镣铐，然后屠杀了整支军队。

sentences.en: Oh, he breaks his word.
sentences.zh: 哦，他背信弃义了。

sentences.en: He does break his word because he says that the murderers of Gisgo were beyond the pale.
sentences.zh: 他确实背信弃义了，因为他说杀害吉斯戈的凶手是不可饶恕的。

sentences.en: That's fair, I think, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很公平，汤姆。

sentences.en: They behave very poorly to Gisgo.
sentences.zh: 他们对吉斯戈的行为太恶劣了。

sentences.en: And to be honest, do you have to keep your word to a mercenary anyway?
sentences.zh: 老实说，你对雇佣兵真的需要信守诺言吗？

sentences.en: Well, so now the war reaches its, can I say, hideous climax, Tom?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那么现在战争达到了，我可以这么说吗，恐怖的高潮，汤姆？

sentences.en: Oh, we love a hideous climax, Tom.
sentences.zh: 哦，我们喜欢恐怖的高潮，汤姆。

sentences.en: A hideous climax.
sentences.zh: 恐怖的高潮。

sentences.en: So Hamilcar and his deputy, inevitably called Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 所以哈米尔卡和他的副手，不可避免地也叫汉尼拔。

sentences.en: But he's not Hannibal, to be clear.
sentences.zh: 但要说明的是，他不是那个汉尼拔。

sentences.en: This is not the famous Hannibal, who we'll be coming to shortly.
sentences.zh: 这不是那位著名的汉尼拔，我们很快就会讲到他。

sentences.en: Hamilcar and his deputy called Hannibal, they march on the remaining army, which is led by Matho, the Libyan, big hairy Libyan.
sentences.zh: 哈米尔卡和他的副手汉尼拔向马托领导的剩余军队进军，那个利比亚人，那个毛发浓密的利比亚人。

sentences.en: And they arrive outside Matho's camp and they put up 10 crosses and they nail Spendius and the other nine ambassadors to the crosses and they kind of leave them there.
sentences.zh: 他们到达马托的营地外，竖起了10个十字架，把斯彭迪乌斯和其他九名使者钉在十字架上，就把他们留在那儿了。

sentences.en: And Matho is so outraged, so appalled, so humiliated that he summons his men and they ambush Hannibal's force
sentences.zh: 马托感到无比愤怒、震惊和羞辱，于是他召集部下伏击了汉尼拔的部队，

sentences.en: and they capture Hannibal and they torture him at the foot of Spendius's cross.
sentences.zh: 俘虏了汉尼拔，并在斯彭迪乌斯的十字架下折磨他。

sentences.en: And they then take down the body of Spendius and they nail Hannibal alive to the cross.
sentences.zh: 然后他们取下斯彭迪乌斯的尸体，把活着的汉尼拔钉在十字架上。

sentences.en: And they take 30 high-ranking Carthaginian prisoners and they sacrifice them at the foot of the cross as a kind of, you know, a sacrifice to the spirit of Spendius.
sentences.zh: 他们还抓了30名迦太基高官作为俘虏，在十字架下将他们献祭，作为一种对斯彭迪乌斯之灵的祭品。

sentences.en: And Hamilcar, in the face of this, has to beat a retreat, but it's fine.
sentences.zh: 面对这种情况，哈米尔卡不得不撤退，但这没关系。

sentences.en: He hasn't suffered any major defeat.
sentences.zh: 他没有遭受任何重大失败。

sentences.en: And he patches things up with Hanno and the two of them advance out again.
sentences.zh: 他与汉诺重修旧好，两人再次出击。

sentences.en: And in the autumn of 238, they meet with the surviving mercenaries and they win an absolutely crushing victory.
sentences.zh: 在公元前238年秋天，他们与幸存的雇佣兵交战，并取得了绝对性的压倒胜利。

sentences.en: Most of the mercenaries are wiped out.
sentences.zh: 大部分雇佣兵被消灭了。

sentences.en: The survivors are all crucified and Matho is taken prisoner.
sentences.zh: 幸存者全部被钉死在十字架上，马托被俘。

sentences.en: So Matho has survived, but his fate is very exciting, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以马托活了下来，但他的下场非常刺激，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He is made to walk through the streets of Carthage in a kind of parody of the triumphal procession that he would have enjoyed had he managed to enter the great city.
sentences.zh: 他被迫走过迦太基的街道，这是一种对他本应在进入这座伟大城市时享受的凯旋游行的讽刺。

sentences.en: And Dominic, I'm sure you'll remember it from reading Salambo.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我相信你读过《萨朗波》一定记得这一幕。

sentences.en: There's a horrible, horrible account of it.
sentences.zh: 那是一段极其恐怖的描写。

sentences.en: It's the kind of, we love a hideous climax.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种，我们喜欢恐怖的高潮。

sentences.en: It's the hideous climax of Salambo.
sentences.zh: 这是《萨朗波》中恐怖的高潮。

sentences.en: And in Flaubert's version of it, it's decreed that he can walk through the streets without an escort, but with his arms tied behind his back.
sentences.zh: 在福楼拜的版本中，规定他可以在没有护卫的情况下走过街道，但双手被反绑在背后。

sentences.en: And the crowds are not allowed to put out his eyes because Matho has to be able to see what is being done to him.
sentences.zh: 人群不允许挖出他的眼睛，因为马托必须能看到别人对他做的事。

sentences.en: And they're not allowed to cripple him because he has to carry on walking.
sentences.zh: 他们不允许弄残他，因为他必须继续走下去。

sentences.en: And they're not allowed to inflict anything that would kill him.
sentences.zh: 他们不允许对他施加任何会让他死去的酷刑。

sentences.en: Anything else, they can do what they want to do.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，他们想做什么都可以。

sentences.en: And so this is Flaubert's description of what happens.
sentences.zh: 这就是福楼拜对所发生之事的描述。

sentences.en: The crowds discharged little drops of boiling oil through tubes at him.
sentences.zh: 人群通过管子向他喷射滚烫的油滴。

sentences.en: They strewed pieces of broken glass beneath his feet.
sentences.zh: 他们在他的脚下撒满碎玻璃。

sentences.en: Still he walked on.
sentences.zh: 他依然向前走着。

sentences.en: The slaves of the council struck him with their whips of hippopotamus leather, so furiously and long that the fringes of their tunics were drenched with sweat.
sentences.zh: 议会的奴隶们用河马皮鞭疯狂地抽打他，时间如此之长，以至于他们长袍的边缘都被汗水浸透了。

sentences.en: Matho appeared insensible.
sentences.zh: 马托看起来毫无知觉。

sentences.en: Suddenly he started off and began to run at random, making a noise with his lips like one shivering with severe cold.
sentences.zh: 突然，他开始胡乱奔跑，嘴唇发出像是在严寒中颤抖的声音。

sentences.en: That's not even the worst bit, Tom.
sentences.zh: 那还不是最糟糕的部分，汤姆。

sentences.en: Do you want to come to the worst bit?
sentences.zh: 你想听听最糟糕的部分吗？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, there's so many bits.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，有太多部分了。

sentences.en: Because Flaubert, as we said in the first episode, he really kind of goes to town on this, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为福楼拜，正如我们在第一集里说的，他真的在这方面大做文章，不是吗？

sentences.en: A child rent his ear.
sentences.zh: 一个孩子撕裂了他的耳朵。

sentences.en: A young girl, hiding the point of a spindle in her sleeve, spit his cheek.
sentences.zh: 一个年轻女孩把纺锤尖藏在袖子里，刺穿了他的脸颊。

sentences.en: They tore handfuls of hair from him.
sentences.zh: 他们成把地扯下他的头发。

sentences.en: I mean, he was very hairy.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他毛发非常浓密。

sentences.en: And strips of flesh.
sentences.zh: 还有皮肉。

sentences.en: Others smeared his face with sponges steeped in filth and fastened upon sticks.
sentences.zh: 其他人用绑在棍子上的海绵蘸着污秽涂抹他的脸。

sentences.en: And then it just kind of goes on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 然后它就这么没完没了地继续下去。

sentences.en: And at the end, Flaubert says at one point, he had no appearance of humanity left.
sentences.zh: 最后，福楼拜在某处写道，他已经看不出人形了。

sentences.en: He was a long, perfectly red shape.
sentences.zh: 他成了一个长长的、完全血红的形状。

sentences.en: I mean, by the standards of 1860s, I don't think it's all about a pulvary, is it?
sentences.zh: 我是说，以1860年代的标准来看，我觉得这不全是关于普尔瓦里，对吧？

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不。

sentences.en: No, I mean, it's not Dickens, even.
sentences.zh: 不，我是说，这甚至不是狄更斯。

sentences.en: So this takes us back to where we began with Flaubert's kind of imagining of Carthage.
sentences.zh: 所以这把我们带回了开头，福楼拜对迦太基的想象。

sentences.en: And of course, we opened the series, Dominic, with Flaubert imagining a sacrifice to Moloch, the Carthaginian elite sacrificing their children in this great blazing furnace,
sentences.zh: 当然，多米尼克，我们在系列节目开头就讲了福楼拜想象中对摩洛克的祭祀，迦太基精英们在这个巨大的燃烧炉中献祭他们的孩子，

sentences.en: which you do at moments of particular peril, because your child, of course, is the most precious thing that you have.
sentences.zh: 这通常是在极度危险的时刻才会做的事，因为孩子当然是你最珍贵的东西。

sentences.en: And in that account, Hamilcar is pressured by the council to sacrifice his eldest son, who, of course, had been born while Hamilcar was in Sicily.
sentences.zh: 在那个记述中，哈米尔卡受到议会的压力，要他献祭长子，那个孩子当然是在哈米尔卡在西西里时出生的。

sentences.en: And this boy was given the name of Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 这个男孩被取名为汉尼拔。

sentences.en: So Hannibal Barker.
sentences.zh: 也就是汉尼拔·巴卡。

sentences.en: And it's an echo of a scene that almost certainly did happen.
sentences.zh: 这是一个几乎肯定发生过的场景的回响。

sentences.en: And it didn't involve Moloch, and it didn't involve human sacrifice, but it did involve sacrifice before the greatest of the gods of Carthage, which was Baal Hamon.
sentences.zh: 它不涉及摩洛克，也不涉及活人祭祀，但它确实涉及在迦太基最伟大的神巴力哈蒙面前的祭祀。

sentences.en: And Hamilcar Barker, he is now the greatest man in Carthage.
sentences.zh: 哈米尔卡·巴卡，他现在是迦太基最伟大的人。

sentences.en: He has won this great victory over the mercenaries.
sentences.zh: 他赢得了对雇佣兵的这场伟大胜利。

sentences.en: He was the last man standing against the Romans in Sicily.
sentences.zh: 他是西西里岛上最后一个对抗罗马人的人。

sentences.en: And yet, at the same time, he has been powerless to oppose the Romans, who were behaving very, very badly.
sentences.zh: 然而与此同时，他却无力阻止那些行为极其恶劣的罗马人。

sentences.en: Even though the Romans did not intervene in the mercenary war, they take advantage of Carthage's distraction to seize Sardinia against the terms of the peace treaty.
sentences.zh: 尽管罗马人没有干预雇佣兵战争，但他们趁迦太基分心，违反和平条约夺取了撒丁岛。

sentences.en: And when the Carthaginians complain, the Romans threaten them with war.
sentences.zh: 当迦太基人抱怨时，罗马人威胁要对他们开战。

sentences.en: So it's like that phrase that the Gauls had said to the Romans when they captured Rome and extorted lots of treasure out of them, woe to the defeated.
sentences.zh: 这就像高卢人在占领罗马并勒索大量财宝时对罗马人说的那句话：失败者有祸了。

sentences.en: And so the Carthaginians have no option but to suck it up.
sentences.zh: 所以迦太基人别无选择，只能忍气吞声。

sentences.en: But obviously, they feel incredible resentment.
sentences.zh: 但显然，他们感到难以置信的怨恨。

sentences.en: And probably there's no one who feels greater resentment than Hamilcar, this great patriotic figure, greatest military leader,
sentences.zh: 可能没有人比哈米尔卡感到更大的怨恨了，这位伟大的爱国人物，最伟大的军事统帅，

sentences.en: the man who dreams of seeing his city restored to her former position as undisputed mistress of the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 那个梦想着看到他的城市恢复昔日作为西方无可争议的女主人地位的人。

sentences.en: And so he knows that he needs to find some way with Sicily off limits, with Sardinia lost, to restore Carthage's fortunes and above all finances.
sentences.zh: 所以他知道，随着西西里岛被限制，撒丁岛丢失，他需要找到某种方法来恢复迦太基的财富，尤其是财政。

sentences.en: And so he looks to Spain because Spain is a place so rich in silver that it is said when there are forest fires on the high slopes of the mountains,
sentences.zh: 于是他看向西班牙，因为西班牙是一个盛产白银的地方，据说当高山斜坡上发生森林火灾时，

sentences.en: liquid silver runs in torrents down the side of the hill.
sentences.zh: 液态的白银会像洪流一样顺着山坡流下。

sentences.en: And so he decides that this is where he's going to go.
sentences.zh: 于是他决定这就是他要去的地方。

sentences.en: He's going to carve out a new empire.
sentences.zh: 他要开辟一个新的帝国。

sentences.en: He sets out for there in 237.
sentences.zh: 他在公元前237年出发前往那里。

sentences.en: But before he leaves, as I say, he goes to offer sacrifice to Balhamon.
sentences.zh: 但在离开之前，正如我所说，他去向巴力哈蒙献祭。

sentences.en: And he takes with him his eldest son, this little boy, Hannibal, who by now is about nine years old.
sentences.zh: 他带着他的长子，这个小男孩汉尼拔，当时大约九岁。

sentences.en: And he offers sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 他进行了献祭。

sentences.en: And the omen's proof favorable.
sentences.zh: 预兆是吉利的。

sentences.en: Balhamon approves of Hamilcar's expedition to Spain.
sentences.zh: 巴力哈蒙赞同哈米尔卡的西班牙远征。

sentences.en: And this then done, Hamilcar orders everyone to withdraw except for his young boy, Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 做完这些后，哈米尔卡命令所有人退下，只留下他的小儿子汉尼拔。

sentences.en: And he calls Hannibal, come and stand by me.
sentences.zh: 他叫道：汉尼拔，过来站在我身边。

sentences.en: And then he says, would you like to come with me to Spain?
sentences.zh: 然后他说：你想和我一起去西班牙吗？

sentences.en: And Hannibal's eyes light up.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔的眼睛亮了起来。

sentences.en: And he says, yes, I would love to come to Spain.
sentences.zh: 他说：是的，我很想去西班牙。

sentences.en: I want to be with you.
sentences.zh: 我想和你在一起。

sentences.en: And Hamilcar nods.
sentences.zh: 哈米尔卡点了点头。

sentences.en: And then he tells his son, lay your hand on the carcass of the sacrificial victim and swear this oath that you will never bear goodwill to the Romans.
sentences.zh: 然后他告诉儿子：把手放在祭品的尸体上，发誓你永远不会对罗马人怀有善意。

sentences.en: And the little boy swears it, but he will never bear goodwill to the Romans.
sentences.zh: 小男孩发了誓，他永远不会对罗马人怀有善意。

sentences.en: And this boy, nine-year-old son of Hamilcar, Hannibal Barker, after Hamilcar goes on to die in Spain, having carved out the great empire that he'd wanted
sentences.zh: 而这个男孩，哈米尔卡九岁的儿子汉尼拔·巴卡，在哈米尔卡死于西班牙、开辟了他想要开辟的伟大帝国之后，

sentences.en: to carve out, Hannibal will succeed to its rule.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔将继承他的统治。

sentences.en: And in due course, he will launch an invasion of Italy itself, leading war elephants over the Alps and bringing the Romans to a succession of terrible defeats
sentences.zh: 在适当的时候，他将发动对意大利本身的入侵，带着战象翻越阿尔卑斯山，给罗马人带来一连串可怕的失败，

sentences.en: and bringing Rome itself to the very brink of utter disaster.
sentences.zh: 并将罗马本身推向彻底灾难的边缘。

sentences.en: And Hannibal will be remembered by the Romans for all time as the greatest of all their enemies.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔将永远被罗马人铭记为他们所有敌人中最伟大的一位。

sentences.en: And Dominic, next year maybe, we will continue the story of Carthage and we will look at the rise to greatness of Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，明年也许我们会继续迦太基的故事，看看汉尼拔如何崛起并走向伟大。

sentences.en: We will indeed.
sentences.zh: 我们确实会。

sentences.en: What a wonderful series, Tom.
sentences.zh: 多么精彩的系列节目，汤姆。

sentences.en: And what an amazing incentive for people to carry on listening to the rest of this history, knowing that one day when they least expect it, Hannibal will be ambushed.
sentences.zh: 这对人们继续收听这段历史的其余部分是一个多么惊人的激励，因为他们知道有一天，当他们最意想不到的时候，汉尼拔会遭到伏击。

sentences.en: So that was a fantastic, a blood-drenched tour de force.
sentences.zh: 那真是一场精彩绝伦、血雨腥风的杰作。

sentences.en: Everything that we wanted from a history of Carthage.
sentences.zh: 我们从迦太基历史中想要的一切都有了。

sentences.en: Tom, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: That was absolutely wonderful.
sentences.zh: 那真是太棒了。

sentences.en: So next week, we have a complete change of tone.
sentences.zh: 所以下周，我们将完全改变基调。

sentences.en: We will be returning with a history of chocolate from its Mesoamerican origins to its glory days in Victorian Birmingham.
sentences.zh: 我们将回归巧克力历史，从它在中美洲的起源一直讲到它在维多利亚时代伯明翰的辉煌岁月。

sentences.en: And then the episode that I think many people have been waiting for, for years, frankly, that you'll only get on the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 还有我认为许多人已经等了多年的一集，坦率地说，你只能在《历史的其余部分》中听到。

sentences.en: And that is, of course, History's Greatest Monkeys.
sentences.zh: 那就是，当然，历史上最伟大的猴子。

sentences.en: So we will see you for those episodes next week.
sentences.zh: 所以我们下周会在这些节目中见到大家。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
